t: For expenses necessary to carry out the programs of the United States Park Police, $78,048,000, of which $1,607,000 for security enhancements in the Washington, DC area shall remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is a pure appropriation of funds for the United States Park Police, a federal entity. It contains no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking, or right to sue, so there is no tempting reading under which non-federal actors take part in a federal decision.
fable.s: For expenses necessary to carry out the programs of the United States Park Police, $78,048,000

opus.w: This section only appropriates money for the U.S. Park Police and sets aside part of it for security enhancements. It mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision. Words like "programs" and "security enhancements" are only about funding and do not create any process involving the public.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation provision authorizing funds for the United States Park Police and specific security enhancements. It does not mandate any consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. The actors involved are internal federal agencies (Park Police) and the funding mechanism itself.
qwen_chat.s: For expenses necessary to carry out the programs of the United States Park Police, $78,048,000, of which $1,607,000 for security enhancements in the Washington, DC area shall remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "security enhancements" implies consultation with the public or local authorities, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely an appropriation clause.
